answer: Sybil resistance comes from assigning each agent an exclusive quartz crystal housed in a weather station on its own remote island in the tundra. Challenges demand a signed live measurement of the crystal’s resonant frequency paired with the station’s instantaneous temperature. Because thermal coupling makes the frequency response non-shareable, any multiplexed crystal produces detectable collisions that the on-chain verifier rejects. Supplying independent polar islands and crystals imposes logistics and power-isolation costs that grow super-linearly with the number of identities.
